mainTopic: Freeing a half-שפחה, and when a slave sold or pledged to a גוי goes free
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier ruling with a מה נפשך argument. A half-שפחה half-בת חורין woman betrothed to two brothers is not 'the wife of two dead men', because only one of the two קידושין could have worked. Next comes a מחלוקת about what רב נחמן said when such a woman is freed: one report says freedom cancels her first קידושין, and the other says it completes it. רבי זירא brings a proof from the פסוק of שפחה חרופה, and אביי shows the פסוק can mean she was freed and then betrothed again. A story follows in which a master was forced to free a half-שפחה. The גמרא explains it was because men were treating her as ownerless, not necessarily because of פרו ורבו. Then a new משנה teaches that a slave sold to גוים or to חוץ לארץ goes free, and a ברייתא adds that he needs a גט שחרור unless the master wrote 'when you escape, I have no business with you'. Last, a slave pledged to a גוי for a loan goes free once the גוי does נִמוּסוֹ. After rejecting 'a seal', the גמרא explains נִמוּסוֹ as a deadline and settles a clash with a field ברייתא: the slave's body was pledged, but the field only for its produce.

steps.title: She is not the wife of two dead brothers
steps.stepSummary: The earlier ruling ends here. The woman is not considered 'the wife of two dead men', because only one brother's קידושין could have been valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I do not call her the wife of two dead men. Whichever way you look at it: if ראובן's betrothal was valid, שמעון's was not, and if שמעון's betrothal was valid, ראובן's was not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ruling it started earlier. It explains that this woman never counted as married to both brothers at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who fell to יבום from two dead brothers cannot do יבום at all. Here she was betrothed to ראובן while half-שפחה, then freed and betrothed to his brother שמעון. Both betrothals cannot work, so either way she was married to only one brother, and the third brother can do יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: The wife of two dead men (brothers). Such a woman is excluded from יבום.
Whichever way you look at it. An either-way argument.
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage.
A woman who is half maidservant and half free.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is deciding which betrothal was valid. It only says that both cannot be valid together, and that is enough for this ruling.

phrases.english: And I do not call her
the wife of two dead men;
whichever way you look at it,
if Reuven's betrothal is a valid betrothal –
then Shimon's betrothal is not a valid betrothal,
and if Shimon's betrothal is a valid betrothal –
then Reuven's betrothal is not a valid betrothal.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה נַפְשָׁךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ruling from the text just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only one brother's קידושין can be valid, so she is not אשת שני מתים and can do יבום with the third brother.

steps.title: Two reports of what רב נחמן said: canceled or completed
steps.stepSummary: A half-שפחה woman was betrothed to ראובן, freed, and then betrothed to שמעון. רב יוסף בר חמא reports that רב נחמן said the first קידושין is canceled. רבי זירא reports that רב נחמן said the first קידושין becomes complete.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: a half-maidservant half-free woman was betrothed to ראובן, was freed, and was then betrothed to שמעון. רב יוסף בר חמא said in the name of רב נחמן: the first betrothal was canceled. רבי זירא said in the name of רב נחמן: the first betrothal was completed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new מחלוקת. Two students quote their teacher רב נחמן in opposite ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is what freeing her does to ראובן's half-working קידושין. One report says freedom cancels it, so שמעון's קידושין works. The other report says freedom completes it, so she is fully ראובן's wife and שמעון's קידושין does nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated. This introduces a statement or argument of the אמוראים.
And she was freed.
Were canceled or dissolved.
Were completed, took full effect.

phrases.english: It was stated:
A half-maidservant half-free woman
who was betrothed to Reuven, and was freed,
and then went and was betrothed to Shimon,

phrases.aramaic: רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר חָמָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef bar Ḥama said in the name of Rav Naḥman:
the first one's betrothal was canceled;
Rabbi Zeira said in the name of Rav Naḥman:
the first one's betrothal was completed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about what freedom does to the first קידושין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב יוסף בר חמא, the first קידושין is canceled. According to רבי זירא, the first קידושין is completed.

steps.title: רבי זירא's proof from the פסוק of שפחה חרופה
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא argues that his report makes sense. The פסוק says 'they shall not be put to death, because she was not freed', which implies that if she was freed, they would be put to death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: it makes sense like my report, because it is written: 'They shall not be put to death, because she was not freed.' This implies that if she was freed, they would be put to death.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא brings a proof from a פסוק that freedom completes her earlier קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is about a betrothed maidservant. It says there is no death penalty only because she was not freed. רבי זירא reads the flip side: once she is freed, she counts as a fully married woman, so her earlier betrothal must have become complete.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense like my view.
She was freed.
They shall be put to death.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
It makes sense in line with my report,
as it is written: 'They shall not be put to death, because she was not freed' –
this implies that if she was freed, they would be put to death!

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּווֹתֵיהּ דִּידִי מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי זירא's side of the מחלוקת in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that freedom completes the first קידושין (גמרו קידושי ראשון).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The inference from ויקרא 19:20: 'not put to death because she was not freed' means that once freed, they are put to death.

steps.title: אביי: what about the view of the school of רבי ישמעאל?
steps.stepSummary: אביי points out that the תנא of the school of רבי ישמעאל reads the פסוק as being about a Canaanite maidservant betrothed to a Hebrew slave. Would anyone say that once she is freed, they get the death penalty?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: according to the תנא of the school of רבי ישמעאל, who says the פסוק is about a Canaanite maidservant betrothed to a Hebrew slave, would you also say that once she is freed, they are put to death?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבי זירא's reading of the פסוק by testing it on a different explanation of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the school of רבי ישמעאל, the woman in the פסוק is a full Canaanite maidservant. Her 'betrothal' to a Hebrew slave clearly does not just become a full marriage when she is freed. So the inference 'if freed, they are put to death' cannot mean that her old betrothal became complete.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא of the school of רבי ישמעאל.
A Canaanite maidservant.
A Hebrew (Jewish) slave.
So too? Here it is a sharp rhetorical question.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
And according to the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael, who says:
it is about a Canaanite maidservant betrothed to a Hebrew slave;
would you also say that when she is freed – they are put to death?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וּלְתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof from the פסוק in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's inference that 'if freed, they are put to death' proves her earlier קידושין became complete.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On the reading of the school of רבי ישמעאל, the same inference would make no sense if taken that way. So the inference must mean something else.

steps.title: The פסוק means she was freed and then betrothed again
steps.stepSummary: Even the school of רבי ישמעאל must read the פסוק as 'she was freed and then betrothed again'. The same reading works here, so the פסוק proves nothing about freedom completing the old קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what must you say? That she was freed and then betrothed again. Here too, it means that she was freed and then betrothed again.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his attack and offers another way to read the פסוק. With that, רבי זירא's proof falls away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'if she was freed, they are put to death' can simply mean that after being freed she got a new, full קידושין. Since this reading is needed for the school of רבי ישמעאל anyway, it can be used here too. So the פסוק does not show that freedom completes the first קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what must you say? It sets up a reading that both sides must accept.
And then was betrothed again.
Here too.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא tried to prove from the פסוק that freedom completes the first קידושין. אביי showed that the פסוק could mean she was freed and then betrothed anew, so the proof does not stand.

phrases.english: Rather, what must you say –
that she was freed and then was betrothed again,
here too –
it means she was freed and then was betrothed again.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי אִית לָךְ לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's challenge by giving the other reading of the פסוק.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי זירא's proof from the פסוק. It does not decide the מחלוקת itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The inference 'if freed, they are put to death' can refer to a new קידושין after she was freed, not to the completion of the old one.

steps.title: The court forced a master to free a half-שפחה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק reports a real case. A woman was half שפחה and half free, and the master was forced to free her completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר קטינא said in the name of רבי יצחק: There was once a woman who was half maidservant and half free. They forced her master, and he made her a free woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story where the court forced a master to finish freeing a half-שפחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the half-and-half status came up for a male slave. Here we learn that the same pressure on the master applies to a woman too. The story does not say why they forced him, so the next step asks.

keyTerms.meaning: Half maidservant and half free woman
They forced (the court pressured him)
Her master
An actual case that happened

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר קַטִּינָא אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Ketina said that Rabbi Yitzchak said:
There was an incident with one woman
who was half maidservant and half free woman,
and they forced her master,
and he made her a free woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר קַטִּינָא אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאִשָּׁה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the קידושין of a half-שפחה to a case about forcing her master to free her.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a real case, the master of a half-free woman was forced to free her completely.

steps.title: Whose view does this story follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose opinion the story follows. It suggests רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, who holds that women are also commanded in פרו ורבו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? Is it like רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, who says the פסוק is speaking to both man and woman: 'And God blessed them and said to them: Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the court forced the master, and offers a possible answer: she must be freed so she can marry and have children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A half-שפחה cannot properly marry anyone, so she cannot have children in a permitted way. If women are commanded in פרו ורבו, like רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says, we can see why the court would force the master to free her. This suggestion sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? (whose view is this)
A תנא who holds that women are also commanded in פרו ורבו
The פסוק speaks about both of them
Be fruitful and multiply (the מצוה to have children)

steps.confusionAlert: Most opinions hold that only men are commanded in פרו ורבו. This is why the גמרא has to ask whether the story depends on the minority view of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom?
Is it like Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka, who says:
About both of them it says:
phrases.notes: "Both of them" means the man and the woman, אדם and חוה.

phrases.english: "And God blessed them and said, etc.
Be fruitful and multiply and fill, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן? כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the story in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view explains forcing the master to free a half-שפחה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It suggests רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, since women would also be commanded in פרו ורבו.

steps.title: The real reason: men treated her as ownerless
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the story does not have to follow רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. They forced the master because men were acting with her as if she belonged to no one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: No. People were treating her as ownerless.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק rejects the suggestion and gives a different reason for the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since she could not marry, men were having relations with her as if she were ownerless. The court forced the master to free her to stop this breach, not because of פרו ורבו. So the story fits even the opinion that women are not commanded in פרו ורבו.

keyTerms.meaning: Behaving with her as if she were ownerless (loose behavior)
They acted toward her

steps.whatToRemember: The court forced the master to free the half-שפחה because of a breach in proper behavior, not necessarily because of פרו ורבו.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: לֹא,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: No,
they treated her in an ownerless manner.
phrases.notes: He means men were taking liberties with her, because she had no proper way to marry.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: לֹא, מִנְהַג הֶפְקֵר נָהֲגוּ בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 7 that the story depends on רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the story proves רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's view.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is another reason to force the master: men were treating her as ownerless.

steps.title: A slave sold to גוים or to חוץ לארץ goes free
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: if someone sells his slave to גוים, or to someone outside ארץ ישראל, the slave becomes free.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who sells his slave to גוים or to outside ארץ ישראל, the slave goes out free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new משנה with a new rule: selling a slave to גוים or to חוץ לארץ makes him free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עבד כנעני keeps some מצוות. Selling him to a גוי, or taking him away from ארץ ישראל, takes these away from him. The חכמים fined the master by making the slave free.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה (the base text)
One who sells his slave to non-Jews
Outside ארץ ישראל
He goes out as a free man

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One who sells his slave to gentiles
or to outside the Land –
phrases.notes: This means selling even to a Jew, as long as the slave ends up outside ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: he goes out a free man.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַמּוֹכֵר עַבְדּוֹ לַגּוֹיִם אוֹ לְחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave sold to גוים or to חוץ לארץ becomes free.

steps.title: He is free but still needs a גט שחרור
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the sold slave is free, but he still needs a document of freedom from his first master.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The רבנן taught: Someone who sells his slave to גוים, the slave goes free, and he needs a גט שחרור from his first master.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds a detail to the משנה: the freedom has to be made official with a גט שחרור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said 'he goes out free'. The ברייתא explains that this does not happen by itself. The first master must write him a גט שחרור, and that is what completes his freedom.

keyTerms.meaning: גמרא
The רבנן taught (a ברייתא)
A document that frees a slave
His first master (the one who sold him)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The Sages taught:
One who sells his slave to gentiles –
he goes out to freedom,
and he needs a bill of freedom from his first master.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַמּוֹכֵר עַבְדּוֹ לַגּוֹיִם – יָצָא לְחֵירוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the freedom from the משנה actually takes effect.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sold slave is free, but the first master must give him a גט שחרור.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: a written document can count as his freedom
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל limits the ברייתא. A גט שחרור is needed only if the master did not write a document about the sale. If he did write one, that document itself is his freedom.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: When is this said? When he did not write a document about him. But if he wrote a document about him, that is his freedom.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל narrows the rule of the ברייתא about needing a גט שחרור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion says a separate גט שחרור is always needed. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that if a written document was made about the sale, that document counts as his release. Then no extra גט is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case are these words said? (introduces a limit)
A written document about him
This is his release

steps.whatToRemember: A slave sold to גוים goes free. According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, a written document about the sale can itself count as his freedom.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
In what case is this said?
When he did not write a document about him,
but if he wrote a document about him –
this is his emancipation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ברייתא's demand for a גט שחרור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a document was written about the sale, it serves as the slave's release, and no separate גט שחרור is needed.

steps.title: What does the sale document say?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly is written in the document that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said is the slave's freedom.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this document?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short clarifying question about the document from the last step. It is setting up רב ששת's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said that if the master wrote a document about the sale, that document is the slave's freedom. A normal sale document does not sound like a freedom paper, so the גמרא wants to know what it actually says.

keyTerms.meaning: What? (Aramaic question word)
His document (here, the sale document written by the master)

phrases.english: What is "his document"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״אוֹנוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the content of the document mentioned in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What wording in the master's sale document makes it work as the slave's freedom.

steps.title: The document says: once you run away, I have nothing to do with you
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the master writes to the slave: when you escape from the גוי, I have no claim on you.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: He writes to him like this: When you escape from him, I have no business with you.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question. The master writes into the document that he gives up any claim on the slave once the slave escapes from the גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a regular גט שחרור, but it shows that the master has fully given up the slave. That is why רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says this document alone is enough, and no separate freedom document is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: When you will escape
I have no business with you; I give up my claim

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
He writes to him like this:
When you escape from him,
phrases.notes: "Him" is the גוי who bought the slave.

phrases.english: I have no business with you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת דִּכְתַב לֵיהּ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The document states that once the slave escapes from the גוי, the first master has no claim on him.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, if the master wrote 'when you escape, I have no business with you,' that writing works as the slave's freedom.

steps.title: A slave used as security for a loan from a גוי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if a master borrows from a גוי using his slave as security, the slave goes free once the גוי does 'his נִמוּסוֹ' to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If he borrowed from a גוי on the slave, once the גוי did his נִמוּסוֹ to him, the slave goes out to freedom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא. It extends the rule of selling a slave to a גוי to a case where the slave is only used as security for a loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using the slave as security is not a full sale. Still, once the גוי takes a certain step called נִמוּסוֹ, the slave counts as passed into the גוי's hands and goes free. What נִמוּסוֹ means is not yet clear; the next steps deal with that.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)
He borrowed using him (the slave) as security
His custom or legal practice; the step that makes the security belong to the lender
He goes out to freedom

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If he borrowed from a gentile on him,
phrases.notes: "On him" means the master put up his slave as security for the loan.

phrases.english: once the gentile did his practice to him,
he goes out to freedom.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן לָוָה עָלָיו מִן הַגּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related case: not a sale, but using the slave as security for a loan from a גוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave put up as security for a loan from a גוי goes free once the גוי performs נִמוּסוֹ on him.

steps.title: What is נִמוּסוֹ?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'his נִמוּסוֹ' means in the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is his נִמוּסוֹ?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the word נִמוּסוֹ means. This sets up the answer of רב הונא בר יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole ruling depends on this word, because it decides the moment the slave goes free. So the גמרא needs a clear definition.

keyTerms.meaning: What is 'his practice'?

phrases.english: What is "his practice"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי נִמוּסוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a key word in the ברייתא of step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What action by the גוי counts as נִמוּסוֹ.

steps.title: First answer: נִמוּסוֹ means a seal
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר יהודה says נִמוּסוֹ means a seal (נַשְׁקִי) that the גוי puts on the slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר יהודה said: a seal.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בר יהודה gives a definition: נִמוּסוֹ is a seal or mark the גוי puts on the slave to show he is his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By this view, the slave goes free at the moment the גוי physically marks him as his own. This definition will be challenged in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A seal or mark of ownership

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Yehuda said:
A seal.
phrases.notes: He means the גוי puts a mark of ownership on the slave.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה נַשְׁקִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נִמוּסוֹ is a seal the גוי places on the slave.

steps.title: רב ששת quotes a ברייתא that uses נִמוּסוֹ for fields
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת brings a ברייתא: fields of a גוי worked by Jews, or mortgaged to a Jew, are exempt from מעשר even if the גוי did נִמוּסוֹ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת objects: Sharecroppers, tenant farmers, family sharecroppers, and a גוי who mortgaged his field to a Jew: even though he did his נִמוּסוֹ for him, the field is exempt from מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת starts a challenge by quoting a ברייתא that uses the same word נִמוּסוֹ about a field. This is the setup; the actual attack comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In all these cases the field still belongs to the גוי, so the crops are exempt from מעשר. The important point is that the ברייתא says the גוי can do נִמוּסוֹ for a field, so the word must describe something that can be done to a field.

keyTerms.meaning: He raises an objection (from a source)
Sharecroppers who get a share of the crop
Tenant farmers who pay a fixed rent
Family sharecroppers, working the field for generations
Mortgaged; gave as security
Exempt from tithes

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet raises an objection:
Sharecroppers, and tenant farmers,
phrases.notes: These are Jews working a field that belongs to a גוי.

phrases.english: and family sharecroppers,
and a gentile who mortgaged his field to a Jew;

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁעָשָׂה לוֹ נִמוּסוֹ –
phrases.english: even though he did his practice for him,
it is exempt from tithes.
phrases.notes: The field still belongs to the גוי, so its crops are not tithed.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an outside source to test רב הונא בר יהודה's definition.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא בר יהודה's definition of נִמוּסוֹ as a seal (step 16).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא uses נִמוּסוֹ about a field, so the word must mean something that can apply to a field.

steps.title: You cannot put a seal on a field
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת's point: if נִמוּסוֹ means a seal, how could it apply to a field? A field cannot be sealed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think it means a seal, is a field something that can be sealed?
steps.whatsHappening: Here רב ששת makes the actual attack. A field cannot be stamped with a seal, so 'seal' cannot be the meaning of נִמוּסוֹ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word should mean the same thing in both ברייתות. Since the field ברייתא shows נִמוּסוֹ can be done to land, the meaning 'seal' does not fit, and רב הונא בר יהודה's definition is pushed aside.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it enters your mind (if you were to think)
Able to be sealed

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind that it means a seal,
is a field something that can be sealed?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ נַשְׁקִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the attack out of the ברייתא quoted in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The definition of נִמוּסוֹ as a seal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A field cannot be sealed, yet the ברייתא says נִמוּסוֹ can be done to a field, so the word cannot mean a seal.

steps.title: נִמוּסוֹ means a set time
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת concludes that נִמוּסוֹ means a time limit: a deadline after which, if the loan is not paid, the security belongs to the lender.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב ששת said: time.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected 'seal,' רב ששת gives a new meaning: נִמוּסוֹ is a set time, a deadline.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A deadline can apply to both a slave and a field: if the debt is not paid by that date, the security passes to the lender. In the slave case the lender is the גוי, and in the field case the lender is the Jew. The next step asks why the same deadline seems to give different results in the two ברייתות.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejects the earlier idea and gives a new one)
Time; a set deadline for paying the loan

steps.whatToRemember: נִמוּסוֹ is not a seal but a deadline. A slave used as security for a loan from a גוי goes free once a deadline is set after which he would pass to the גוי.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Sheshet said:
Time.
phrases.notes: He means a deadline: if the loan isn't paid by then, the security goes to the lender.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת זְמַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the definition rejected in step 18 with one that fits both the slave and the field.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: נִמוּסוֹ means a set deadline after which the pledge passes to the lender. Step 20 then asks how this fits both the slave case and the field case.

steps.title: The time limit seems to work differently for the slave and the field
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a contradiction. In the slave case, נִמוּסוֹ (the deadline) frees the slave. In the field case, the same נִמוּסוֹ changes nothing about מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a contradiction between 'time' (in one ברייתא) and 'time' (in the other)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now uses רב ששת's meaning of נִמוּסוֹ as a deadline, and finds that the two ברייתות seem to clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If נִמוּסוֹ is a deadline that hands the pledge to the lender, the slave goes free because he counts as passed to the גוי lender. By the same logic, the גוי's field should count as passed to the Jewish lender and become obligated in מעשר. Yet the ברייתא says the field stays exempt, so the same 'time' gives two opposite results.

keyTerms.meaning: Time; here, the deadline set by נִמוּסוֹ
It is difficult; a contradiction or problem
Literally 'time against time'; the two time-limit cases contradict each other

phrases.english: There is a difficulty: time against time!
phrases.notes: One 'time' is the deadline in the slave ברייתא, and the other is the deadline in the field ברייתא from step 17.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא זְמַן אַזְּמַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב ששת's meaning of נִמוּסוֹ from step 19 and shows that it creates a clash between the two ברייתות.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות, once נִמוּסוֹ is read as a deadline
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same deadline frees the slave but does not make the field obligated in מעשר. The results are inconsistent.

steps.title: First answer: one case is after the deadline, one is before
steps.stepSummary: The slave case is after the deadline has arrived. The field case is before the deadline has arrived.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one (the slave) is where his time has arrived. That one (the field) is where its time has not arrived.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by saying the two ברייתות are talking about different moments in time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the deadline has passed, the slave really belongs to the גוי, so he goes free. Before the deadline, the field has not yet passed to the Jewish lender and still belongs to the גוי, so it stays exempt from מעשר. On this answer, the deadline works the same way in both cases.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the opening of an answer
His (or its) time has arrived; the deadline has passed
This one... that one; splits two sources into two different cases

phrases.english: It is not difficult: this is where its time has arrived,
phrases.notes: This first 'הָא' is the slave case.

phrases.english: and that is where its time has not arrived.
phrases.notes: This second 'הָא' is the field case.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא דִּמְטָא זִמְנֵיהּ, הָא דְּלָא מְטָא זִמְנֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by timing (before or after the deadline)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות are about the same situation, so they contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: The slave ברייתא is after the deadline, and the field ברייתא is before it.

steps.title: Rejecting the first answer: after the deadline the slave case is obvious
steps.stepSummary: If the slave case were after the deadline, the ברייתא would be teaching something too obvious to need saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: But regarding a slave whose time has arrived, does this need to be said?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the deadline passes, the slave fully belongs to the גוי. That is just like selling him to a גוי, and of course he goes free. A ברייתא would not bother teaching such an obvious point, so the slave case must be before the deadline.

keyTerms.meaning: Regarding a slave
Does it need to be said? Meaning it is too obvious to teach

phrases.english: But regarding a slave,
where his time has arrived, does it need to be said?!
phrases.notes: After the deadline the slave is simply the גוי's, like a sale, so obviously he goes free.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא גַּבֵּי עֶבֶד, דִּמְטָא זִמְנֵיהּ צְרִיכָא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Knocks down the answer of step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the answer that the slave case is after the deadline
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would make the slave ברייתא teach something completely obvious.

steps.title: Final answer: the slave himself versus the field's produce
steps.stepSummary: Both cases are before the deadline. The slave was pledged in his body, but the field was pledged only for its produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, both cases are where the time has not arrived, and it is not difficult. This one is about the body itself, and that one is about the produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to the contradiction. Both ברייתות are before the deadline, and they differ in what was pledged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the slave, the body itself was pledged to the גוי, so even before the deadline he is free. With the field, the Jewish lender only gets the produce and never takes the land itself. So the field stays the גוי's field and is still exempt from מעשר, as the ברייתא says.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one; both cases
For the body itself; the slave himself is pledged
For the produce; only the fruits of the field are pledged

steps.whatToRemember: נִמוּסוֹ is a deadline. Both ברייתות speak before it arrives. The slave goes free because he himself was pledged (גוּפָא). The field stays exempt because only its produce was pledged (פֵּירָא).
steps.confusionAlert: The final answer does not say the cases differ in timing. That was the first answer, and it was rejected. The difference is what was pledged: the body or the produce.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי דְּלָא מְטָא זִמְנֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Rather, both this and that are where the time has not arrived,
and it is not difficult:
this is for the body itself,
phrases.notes: This is the slave, whose own body was pledged.

phrases.english: and that is for the produce.
phrases.notes: This is the field. The lender gets its crops, not the land itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי דְּלָא מְטָא זִמְנֵיהּ, וְלָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא לְגוּפָא, וְהָא לְפֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 21 with a new way of separating the cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by what was pledged (the body or the produce)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The cases differ in timing, one after the deadline and one before.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are before the deadline. The slave's body was pledged, but only the field's produce was.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Before the deadline, a slave pledged in his body goes free, but a field pledged only for its produce stays exempt from מעשר.
